verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 9, 10, 11: flat concrete terrace finished with patterned floor tiles, surrounded by masonry parapet; no slope, sheets or roof tiles visible.
verdicts.rationale: Roof photos clearly show a flat RCC terrace consistent with 'RCC Flat Roof'.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: The obstructions on the roof are sky light, solar water
verdicts.photo_observation: Glass skylight visible on upper roof (p9 right, p10/p11 lower-left); dark solar water heater unit visible near parapet (p9 top-right) and modelled in 3D layout (p17-18); headroom with two water tanks (p10/p11 'ashirvad' tank) also present.
verdicts.rationale: Skylight and solar water heater both visible/modelled as stated; headroom + water tanks are an additional obstruction not mentioned in the answer but the array is laid out clear of them.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: Flat roof (no existing slope). Ballast drawing p19: rear leg 0.40 m post + 0.28 m block vs front 0.17 m + 0.28 m block, i.e. ~0.23 m rise over ~1.1 m array depth (~10-12 deg). 3D render p17-18 shows a low tilt.
verdicts.rationale: Low tilt on ballast over a flat roof is consistent with a 10 deg design angle; exact tilt cannot be measured from photos as panels are not yet installed.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: Site layout p17-18 shows a single 8-module row (9.21 m x 2.39 m) on the upper roof only; the lower terrace has no modules. Proposed PV Area p11 marks one area.
verdicts.rationale: Single array on a single roof, matching '1'.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.designer_notes: Ballast Structure with 0.45 m front clearance
verdicts.photo_observation: p19 drawing captioned 'Ballast Structure with 0.45 m front clearance' shows cylindrical ballast blocks (0.28 m) with posts (0.17 m front / 0.40 m rear); front 0.17+0.28 = 0.45 m. Flat tiled terrace (no anchoring needed).
verdicts.rationale: Ballast drawing and dimensions directly match the answer and note.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: Top view p17 with north arrow up: module row runs east-west along the northern edge of the roof, with tanks/skylight/water heater to the south. Tilt direction is not explicitly marked in renders; no compass photo.
verdicts.rationale: E-W row on the north side of the roof is consistent with south-facing modules; tilt direction itself is not explicitly shown.

verdicts.question: How can the roof be accessed?
verdicts.photo_observation: Internal staircase (p7, p9) reaches the lower terrace via a door (p8 top); a fixed steel ladder (p8 bottom, also drawn in 3D p17-18) leads from the lower terrace to the upper roof where the array goes.
verdicts.rationale: The array roof is reached via the fixed ladder as stated (staircase covers only the lower levels).

verdicts.question: Is the building currently under construction?
verdicts.photo_observation: Exterior (p5, p19): finished brick-cladding facade, painted walls, fitted windows, landscaping; interior (p7) finished stairs and flooring. Cranes in p9 background belong to neighbouring sites.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run - from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel - with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target - the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: DC (red) + earthing (green) run along the upper-roof parapet (p11-12) to the headroom wall entry hole (p13 top) and into the inverter room (p13/15). AC (purple) leaves the inverter into a client-laid conduit (p14 top) - its path down to the ground-floor meter is not traced in any photo. Earthing/LA (green/orange) run down the exterior wall (p14 bottom) to the side-yard pits (p15-16). Solar meter -> main meter link drawn on p16. Existing loose cables and a bagged junction hang on the headroom wall at the entry point (p13 top). No conduit/clipping detail shown.
verdicts.rationale: Roof-to-inverter and earthing runs are continuous, but the inverter-to-meter AC segment is concealed/untraced and conduit/clamping is not documented.
